title: Co layer Thickness Driven Structural Evolution and Magnetic Behaviour of Co/Ir/Co Trilayers
authors: Subhavenkadesh SS, Dushyant Singh, Tharundev V, Subha Maity, Navneet Sharma, Vigneshwari SR, Krista R. Khiangte
abstract: Ferromagnetic heavy-metal (FM/HM) trilayer heterostructures provide a versatile platform for investigating the interplay between structural and magnetic properties. In this study, we investigate the effect of Co-layer thickness on the structural and magnetic properties of sputter-deposited $\mathrm{Co}(t_{\mathrm{Co}})/\mathrm{Ir}(5\,\mathrm{nm})/\mathrm{Co}(t_{\mathrm{Co}})$ varying from 2 to 10 nm. Structural characterization using grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXRD) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) reveals a nanocrystalline structure, with the crystallite size increasing with Co-layer thickness. Furthermore, X-ray reflectivity (XRR) reveals a thickness-dependent variation in interface morphology, with the interface roughness ratio reaching a maximum at $t_{\mathrm{Co}} = 4$ nm. Temperature-dependent zero-field-cooled and field-cooled (ZFC-FC) magnetization measurements reveal thickness-dependent characteristic temperatures and multiple relaxation regimes in selected samples, indicating complex thermally activated magnetic behaviour. In contrast, field-dependent hysteresis measurements reveal that the saturation magnetization increases with Co-layer thickness, whereas the coercivity exhibits a pronounced non-monotonic variation, with enhanced values at intermediate thicknesses. Moreover, low-temperature hysteresis loops display thickness-dependent exchange-bias-like shifts, particularly for $t_{\mathrm{Co}} = 2$-$4$ nm. These findings highlight the strong influence of Co-layer thickness on the structural and magnetic properties of Co/Ir/Co trilayers.
summary: This work systematically examines the structural and magnetic properties of Co/Ir/Co trilayers by varying the thickness of the outer Co layers. Using advanced characterization techniques, the authors demonstrate that $t_{Co}$ strongly controls the film's microstructure, leading to measurable changes in magnetic parameters like saturation magnetization and coercivity. The findings highlight the critical role of interface quality and film thickness in tailoring magnetic behavior for spintronic applications.
main_problem: The study investigates how varying the thickness of the Co layer influences the structural evolution and resulting magnetic properties of Co/Ir/Co trilayers.
main_result: The Co-layer thickness strongly dictates the material's properties, leading to thickness-dependent saturation magnetization, non-monotonic coercivity, and complex thermally activated magnetic behavior.
method: The research employs a combination of structural characterization techniques (GIXRD, XRR, HRTEM) and magnetic measurements (ZFC-FC, M-H loops) on sputter-deposited films.
model_or_system: The physical system is a Co(t_Co)/Ir(5nm)/Co(t_Co) trilayer heterostructure, where the thickness of the outer Co layers ($t_{Co}$) is systematically varied from 2 nm to 10 nm.
key_observables: Saturation magnetization ($M_s$), coercivity ($H_c$), crystallite size, interface roughness ratio, and blocking temperature ($T_b$).
important_parameters: Co-layer thickness ($t_{Co}$), Ir spacer thickness (fixed at 5 nm), and temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on interpreting diffraction peaks (GIXRD) to estimate crystallite size and using XRR to quantify interface morphology.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate GIXRD profiles showing peak overlap, crystallite size vs. $t_{Co}$, XRR patterns showing Kiessig fringes, and HRTEM images comparing microstructure at different thicknesses.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents structural characterization (GIXRD, XRR, HRTEM) to map out how $t_{Co}$ affects microstructure, followed by magnetic measurements (ZFC-FC, M-H) to correlate these structural changes with magnetic responses.
why_interesting: While primarily condensed matter magnetism, the study of thickness-dependent magnetic switching and interfacial effects is foundational to understanding quantum phenomena in nanoscale magnetic systems, which is relevant to spintronics and quantum memory.
